title: AGI: The Path Forward – Jason Warner & Eiso Kant, Poolside
talk_summary: This is a Poolside product demo and company pitch: they show their in-house model converting an ADA codebase to Rust inside VS Code, running tests, and adding a feature, then discuss their RL+next-token-prediction thesis and future compute.

takeaways.technique: Permission-scoped agent execution in high-consequence environments
takeaways.what_they_do: They describe deliberately ratcheting down agent permissions rather than letting agents roam freely, because their customers' environments (defense/government) forbid broad data access.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can't have an agent that's just going to run around and do stuff... You need to have the right permissions. You got to actually really ratchet these things down

takeaways.technique: Agent writes and runs its own verification scripts before reporting done
takeaways.what_they_do: The agent, after generating ~1150 lines, wrote bash commands to test its own output and produced a summary; the humans then re-ran the build to confirm.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it actually wrote some bell commands to test it. And when we check out the output of those, this actually looks pretty good.
